items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We started doing a group called the Timeless Allstars, which was put together by Cedar [Walton] and Harold, Curtis Fuller, Billy, Buster, traveling all over Europe.

ctx.x: Waiting. That’s George on there. Cedar Walton did all the arrangements.
You seem to have very special relationships with pianists and also great affinities with drummers. I’m looking at your discography, and I see that you recorded with Roy Haynes back in 1977.

items.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I also produced uh, two for Bobby Hutcherson... So I sort of volunteered... we got together and came out with some pretty good products.

ctx.x: Yeah, we went through L.A., we ended up over here.

Produced by George Butler and Cedar Walton. You see that? George was out takin' a ride probably in one of his car collections. Same thing on this one, yeah. So uh, I, oh man, when I, when I realized uh, the, uh, uh … uh, the, the, the, uh, uh advantage you had by producing and uh, uh orchestrating and doing everything, uh, and how much it paid during these days, I said, "My God, I can't even, again I couldn't tell my fellow musicians what I was doing, financial- wise. It was pretty lucrative, you know, to do…
What was your thinking musically on these projects?
